1.title: Experience, Strategy and Transformation Terms
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Experience, Strategy and Transformation Terms. It covers the exam area Key eye til terms and definitions. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Experience terms. Strategy terms. Transformation terms. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Key eye til terms and definitions (thirty percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: Experience terms
1.text: Experience terms. Experience. How a person perceives and feels about interactions over time. Digital experience. The experience of interacting through digital channels and products. Trust. Confidence that a provider or product will behave as promised. User experience (U X). The experience of a user while using a product or service. Customer experience (C X). The whole experience of a customer with the organization, from first contact on. Experience level agreement (X L A). An agreement on the experience people should have, measured by how they feel, alongside service levels. Human-centered design. Designing around people's needs and behavior, testing with them, and improving. Exam tip: U X equals the person using it. C X equals the person buying and relating to the organization. X L A (experience level agreement) equals experience target; S L A (service level agreement) equals performance target.

1.title: Strategy terms
1.text: Strategy terms. Strategy. The plan for how an organization will achieve its objectives. Business strategy. The strategy of the whole organization (where to compete, how to win). Digital strategy. How the organization will use digital technology to achieve its business strategy. Mission. What the organization does and for whom (today). Vision. The future the organization wants to reach. Purpose. Why the organization exists. voo ka (volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous). An environment that is Volatile, Uncertain, Complex and Ambiguous. Leadership. Guiding and inspiring people toward a shared direction.

1.title: Strategy terms, continued
1.text: Strategy terms. The figure shows this: Purpose, vision, mission and strategy: why, where, what and how. Exam tip: Purpose equals why. Vision equals where we want to be. Mission equals what we do. Strategy equals how we will get there. voo ka is the setting, not a plan.

1.title: Transformation terms
1.text: Transformation terms. Change. The addition, modification or removal of anything that could affect products or services. Transformation. A major, fundamental shift in how an organization works or creates value. Business as usual (B A U). The normal, day-to-day running of the organization. A transformation often needs many changes; once it lands, the new way becomes B A U (business as usual). Exam tip: When a question gives a short definition, match the keyword: "future" is vision, "why" is purpose, "feel" is experience, "normal running" is B A U.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which term describes an environment that is volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: voo ka. voo ka stands for volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A retailer measures how happy shoppers feel after a support chat and agrees a target for it. Which concept is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: An experience level agreement. An X L A sets targets for the experience, measured by how people feel.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statement is C O R R E C T? (one) Vision is the future the organization wants to reach. (two) Purpose is why the organization exists. (three) Mission is the plan to reach the vision. (four) Strategy is the day-to-day running of the organization. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: one and two. Vision is the future and purpose is why it exists.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). blank is the normal, day-to-day operation of an organization. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Business as usual. That is business as usual.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team studies how users behave, builds prototypes with them, and revises the design. Which concept does this describe? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Human-centered design. Human-centered design builds around people's needs and tests with them.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which term covers how an organization will use digital technology to reach its business goals? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Digital strategy. A digital strategy links technology to the business strategy.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does X L A stand for? Answer: Experience level agreement. Question two. What does voo ka stand for? Answer: Volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous. Question three. What is the difference between U X and C X? Answer: U X is a user's experience of using something; C X is a customer's whole experience with the organization.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Purpose answers which question? Answer: Why does the organization exist? Question five. What is change? Answer: The addition, modification or removal of anything that could affect products or services. Question six. What is transformation? Answer: A major shift in how an organization works or creates value.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Experience: U X (user), C X (customer), X L A (experience target), trust, human-centered design. Direction: purpose equals why, vision equals where, mission equals what, strategy equals how. voo ka: volatile, uncertain, complex, ambiguous. Change: add, modify or remove something that could affect products or services. Transformation or B A U: major shift or normal running.
